messages.subject: Re: Thurnstonian IRT models in mirt?
parts:
On Sun, Jan 28, 2018 at 9:15 AM, Dimitrios Zacharatos <sedz...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks for the package, I have spent some months in the past working with it and it saved me a lot of time (time here measured in months or years). I personally find it easy to work with it, however, I was thinking of ways to stress the package in terms of model specifications.

I was wondering if there is any way (1) to fix eta errors to 1 (2) fix item covariances to minus and (3) define errors in terms of Ψ1^2+Ψ2^2 (see screenshot)

Categorical response data do not have unique residual terms (unlike linear regression models with continuous random variables, they are fully determined by the model expected values). This also means that there's no such thing as a 'residual covariance' parameter as well, though you can make similar specifications by realising that residual correlations are equivalent to having a new latent trait that uniquely loads on the variables that appear to correlate (think a much larger bifactor model).  
 

Provided the model in the screenshot by Dr. Anna Brown (2010). I tried to create a similar model specification in mirt.

bimodel<-'eta1=1,2,4,5,7,8
                 eta2=1,3,4,6,7,9
                 eta3=2,3,5,6,8,9
                 COV=eta1*eta2*eta3,1*2*3,4*5*6,7*8*9
          '
I am certain that my model specification is not correct. And I am not sure if COV=1*2*3... is right although a model with such specification runs without complaints.

It isn't, for reasons stated above. Likely the 1*2*3 etc are just ignored because there's no associated factor to match. 


So I was wondering if there is any way in mirt to
1. Fix covariances between items to correlate in a specific direction?

Yes, you'd either need to define the LBOUND/UBOUND terms in your mirt.model definition, or may prefer to to modify the starting values matrix mirt(..., pars = 'values'), set new starting values with the correct signs, and impose upper/lower bound constraints. 
 
2. Fix errors in terms Ψ1^2+Ψ2^2

Not relevant, see above.  

3. Fix error terms of eta's to 1

Also not relevant. 
 

Weather anyone can answer on this or not. I would like to thank you again for the package. I don't know what I would do without it.
